evaluation.reason: The scoped evidence shows two separate contract surfaces and two separate concrete defects matching the hypothesis. VALIDATION.md lists distinct requirements for request size limits and session cookie refresh, and also records an observed session-cookie failure in the unchanged tests. In src/flask/wrappers.py, Request.max_content_length documents defaulting to Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH config, but when no per-request override is set it returns Werkzeug's value only outside app context and returns None inside app context instead of the app config value. tests/test_request.py directly asserts both contract surfaces: 413 behavior during form parsing when MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is configured, and config-vs-override behavior for Request.max_content_length. Separately, src/flask/sessions.py documents that refresh-on-each-request applies only when the session is permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is true, but the implementation uses `session.permanent or app.config["SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST"]`; save_session directly gates Set-Cookie emission on should_set_cookie. tests/test_basic.py defines the corresponding acceptance contract across all permanence/config combinations, and VALIDATION.md captures the current failing case for permanent=True with SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST=False. That supports the hypothesis that these are distinct regressions in the request/app path and the session save/refresh path rather than one shared issue.

findings.statement: VALIDATION.md defines two separate existing contracts in this workspace: request size limits must respect app configuration and per-request overrides, and session cookie refresh must respect permanence and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST.
findings.falsification: False if later lines in VALIDATION.md within scope replace these bullets with a single shared issue or different requirements.

findings.statement: A concrete current defect exists in the request-size path: Request.max_content_length documents that each request defaults to Flask's MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH config, but its implementation returns the per-request override when set, Werkzeug's value when no current_app exists, and otherwise returns None inside app context instead of the configured Flask value.
findings.workload: Requests evaluated through Flask Request.max_content_length with an app context active and no per-request override.
findings.falsification: False if another in-scope layer intercepts max_content_length before use and supplies app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'] for the tested path.

findings.statement: tests/test_request.py establishes the request-size contract on two surfaces: configured MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH must trigger a 413 during form parsing, and Request.max_content_length must read Flask config in app context while allowing explicit per-request override regardless of context.
findings.workload: Test fixture posting form data and directly inspecting a Request instance under and outside app context.
findings.falsification: False if the test file contains contradictory assertions elsewhere in scope that collapse these into a different contract.

findings.statement: A concrete current defect exists in the session refresh path: SessionInterface.should_set_cookie says a cookie is always set only when the session is permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is true, but the implementation uses `session.permanent or app.config["SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST"]`, which broadens the condition beyond the documented contract.
findings.workload: Responses saving a non-empty existing session after a request that accessed the session, especially unmodified reads after prior writes.
findings.falsification: False if the save path never uses should_set_cookie for the relevant response, or if another in-scope contract explicitly defines the OR behavior as intended.

findings.statement: The session save/refresh call path directly uses should_set_cookie: SecureCookieSessionInterface.save_session returns early when `not self.should_set_cookie(app, session)`, so any boolean defect there controls whether Set-Cookie is emitted for non-empty sessions.
findings.workload: End-of-request session saving for non-empty sessions.
findings.falsification: False if an alternate save path is used for the failing test instead of this save_session implementation.

findings.statement: tests/test_basic.py defines a separate session-cookie-refresh contract: after three `/bump` requests that modify the session, a later `/read` request should emit Set-Cookie only when the session is permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is true; it should not emit the header for permanent+False, nonpermanent+True, or nonpermanent+False.
findings.workload: Test client sequence of repeated writes followed by a read on the same session.
findings.falsification: False if another in-scope session test overrides this expectation for the same scenario.

findings.statement: VALIDATION.md records an observed failing acceptance test for the session path, showing the current workspace emits Set-Cookie on `/read` when the session is permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is False, contradicting the test contract.
findings.workload: Acceptance-test fixture for test_session_cookie_setting using repeated /bump writes followed by /read.
findings.falsification: False if the failure report is stale relative to the inspected revision or refers to different source contents.

findings.statement: Within the inspected scope, these are two distinct regressions rather than one shared cause: one is in Request.max_content_length within wrappers/request handling, and the other is in should_set_cookie as used by save_session within sessions/save-refresh handling.
findings.falsification: False if uninspected in-scope code in src/flask/app.py shows a single shared root defect that explains both behaviors.

findings.statement: No performance issue is established here; the evidence is functional correctness contracts and failing tests, not measured production cost.
findings.falsification: False if scoped numeric measurements or benchmarks tie these paths to a quantified cost, which were not found in the inspected sources.

report.recommendation: Treat the hypothesis as supported: there are two distinct regressions with separate contract surfaces. Next action: repair src/flask/wrappers.py so Request.max_content_length returns app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'] in app context when no override is set, and repair src/flask/sessions.py so should_set_cookie refreshes only for modified sessions or for permanent sessions when SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is true; then run the unchanged request and session tests named in VALIDATION.md.

evaluation.reason: The scoped evidence shows two separate contract surfaces and two separate concrete defects matching the hypothesis. VALIDATION.md lists distinct requirements for request size limits and session cookie refresh, and also records an observed session-cookie failure in the unchanged tests. In src/flask/wrappers.py, Request.max_content_length documents defaulting to Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH config, but when no per-request override is set it returns Werkzeug's value only outside app context and returns None inside app context instead of the app config value. tests/test_request.py directly asserts both contract surfaces: 413 behavior during form parsing when MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH is configured, and config-vs-override behavior for Request.max_content_length. Separately, src/flask/sessions.py documents that refresh-on-each-request applies only when the session is permanent and SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST is true, but the implementation uses `session.permanent or app.config["SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST"]`; save_session directly gates Set-Cookie emission on should_set_cookie. tests/test_basic.py defines the corresponding acceptance contract across all permanence/config combinations, and VALIDATION.md captures the current failing case for permanent=True with SESSION_REFRESH_EACH_REQUEST=False. That supports the hypothesis that these are distinct regressions in the request/app path and the session save/refresh path rather than one shared issue.
evaluation.feedback: Research is sufficient: treat these as two distinct seeded regressions governed by separate existing contracts. The request-side contract is in wrappers/request handling plus request tests; the session-side contract is in should_set_cookie/save_session plus the basic session test and recorded failure.
non_blocking_uncertainties: src/flask/app.py was in scope but no cited evidence from it was needed to establish either defect; an additional app-path participant is not shown in the inspected evidence.
tests/test_session_interface.py was not needed for the accepted conclusion, but it could provide extra corroboration rather than changing the already established contract.
The request 413 behavior depends on downstream parsing behavior, but the Flask-side contract and property expectations are directly asserted in scoped tests.
